sources.title: Jules FAQ
sources.locator: Leave while working; Failure handling; Training; Free access
sources.finding: Jules can work after the user leaves the app, notifies plan/task completion, retries failed steps and never trains on private repository content. A recurring no-cost plan is documented. Setup scripts do not support long-lived servers.

sources.title: Jules Limits and Plans
sources.finding: Free, Pro and Ultra document daily limits of 15/100/300 and concurrent limits of 3/15/60. Paid Google AI plans require individual Gmail accounts; business/Workspace upgrade routes are not yet available.

sources.title: Jules Environment setup
sources.finding: Repository setup scripts install dependencies and run discrete checks. Successful Run and Snapshot captures the environment for future tasks, including preinstalled runtimes and tools.

sources.title: Reviewing Jules code
sources.finding: Jules exposes activity/errors, per-file and expanded diffs, real-time feedback, downloadable changes and a completion summary with runtime, files, lines and branch/commit details. Publish branch/PR controls export changes.

sources.title: Jules REST API
sources.finding: Alpha REST API uses X-Goog-Api-Key, with up to three keys. Sessions and activities expose plans, messages and progress. Alpha specifications and keys may change.

sources.title: Repoless, outputs and activity filters
sources.finding: REST API can start sessions without a repository and return changed-file outputs in Git patch format. Activities are immutable records with timestamp filters and can reconstruct a session.

sources.title: Jules Planning
sources.finding: Jules creates a step plan after setup and revises it from chat feedback. Approve plan starts execution, but the documentation says a timer may auto-approve when the user leaves.

sources.title: Jules Errors and failures
sources.finding: Failed steps are retried where possible, including network/install faults. Persistent failures get a failed state and UI badge. Humans can change setup/prompt and rerun.

sources.title: Jules gains memory
sources.finding: Jules saves preferences, nudges and corrections during a task and references them in later same-repository tasks. Memory can be toggled per repository under Knowledge in repo settings.

sources.title: Jules CI Fixer and authorship
sources.finding: Jules receives failed GitHub Actions checks on its own PRs, fixes and resubmits. User-level settings choose Jules-only, coauthored or user-only commits.

sources.title: Jules web-app testing
sources.finding: Jules can render and verify a frontend, returning a screenshot with the code changes. The base image includes Playwright.

sources.title: Google Terms linked from Jules
sources.locator: Jules homepage Terms of Service link; Google service/software permissions and intellectual property
sources.finding: The Jules homepage links Google Terms of Service for its hosted application. These are vendor-authored service/software terms retaining Google intellectual-property rights, not an open-source grant for the hosted coding agent. Public SDK or example repositories do not establish the core service license.

sources.title: Jules Tools remote-session architecture
sources.finding: Jules Tools is a local npm CLI/TUI for Google-authenticated remote sessions. It controls the Google-hosted Jules worker rather than executing the coding agent on the client or a user server.

sources.title: Jules API resource scope
sources.finding: The documented primary API resources are sources, sessions and session activities. This establishes a session/run API, but not independent issue-backlog records, human workspace roles or a shared-human prompting model.

sources.title: Jules Getting started
sources.locator: Login; Connect GitHub; Starting your first task; Include AGENTS.md file; Enabling notifications
sources.finding: Users sign in with a Google account, connect GitHub and choose repositories, pick a repo and branch, write a prompt and request a plan to approve. Jules reads AGENTS.md at the repository root. Browser notifications report completion or a need for input.

sources.title: Running Tasks with Jules
sources.locator: Choose a repo and branch; Write a clear prompt; Attach visual context; Watching Jules work; Final summary; Giving feedback mid-task; Pausing Jules; Starting tasks from GitHub Issues
sources.finding: Tasks start from a plain-language prompt in the web prompt box on a chosen repo and branch, with optional PNG/JPEG images (under 5 MB) that are never committed. An activity feed, mini diffs and a diff editor show progress; chat feedback mid-task makes Jules replan. Tasks can be paused. Adding the jules label to a GitHub issue starts a task; Jules comments on the issue and links the resulting pull request.

sources.title: Managing tasks and repos
sources.locator: Starting tasks; Pausing or deleting tasks; Managing repositories
sources.finding: Several tasks can run simultaneously, each in its own VM with its own logs, environment setup and code changes. Paused tasks can be resumed; deleted tasks are removed permanently. Jules can only access GitHub repositories the user explicitly allows; other version control systems are future work.

sources.title: Jules Repo view
sources.finding: The repo view lists running tasks first, completed tasks with full logs and diffs, and clearly labelled failed or waiting tasks; any task can be reopened to review its plan or continue feedback.

sources.title: Jules Limits and Plans
sources.locator: Plan Availability note; Plan Comparison; FAQ
sources.finding: Plans allow 15/100/300 tasks per rolling 24 hours and 3/15/60 concurrent tasks (Jules, Pro, Ultra), all with Gemini models. Paid plans come with Google AI Pro/Ultra and are only for individual @gmail.com accounts; business users fill an interest form. Family plan members each get their own limits. Users must be 18 or older. At the daily limit new tasks are blocked while existing tasks remain accessible.

sources.title: Jules FAQ
sources.locator: What is Jules?; Is Jules available without cost?; How does Jules work under the hood?; security; Can I leave Jules while its working?; What happens if a task fails?; Does Jules train on private repos?
sources.finding: Jules is in Public Beta and includes a no-cost plan. Each task runs in a fresh cloud VM with internet access where Jules clones the repo and installs dependencies. Users can leave the app after submitting a task. Failed tasks are retried automatically, then marked failed with a notification.

sources.title: Jules Environment setup
sources.locator: intro; Add a setup script; Test your setup script; Environment Snapshots
sources.finding: Each task runs in a secure, short-lived Ubuntu VM. Without a script Jules studies the repository and uses AGENTS.md or README.md for setup hints; setup scripts can be validated with Run and Snapshot, and the snapshot is reused by later tasks in that repository.

sources.title: Reviewing code changes
sources.locator: Activity feed; Code diffs; Interactive feedback; Task summary; Pushing to GitHub
sources.finding: A real-time activity feed logs steps, outputs, errors and requests for feedback; the diff editor shows all changed files with download and copy. Publish branch or Publish PR pushes to GitHub, after which users review and merge the PR themselves.

sources.title: Reviewing plans & giving feedback
sources.finding: Jules presents a step-by-step plan for approval; feedback in chat makes it update the plan. If the user navigates away, the plan is auto-approved on a timer.

sources.title: Jules Errors and failures
sources.locator: How errors are reported; Automatic retry behavior; Debugging environment setup
sources.finding: Errors appear in the activity feed and as a red notification badge; transient failures are retried, persistent ones mark the task failed; users can rerun from the task summary after editing the setup script or prompt.

sources.title: Jules Suggested Tasks
sources.locator: Enabling Suggested Tasks; Reviewing and Running Suggestions; Feedback and Dismissal
sources.finding: Proactivity scans up to five repositories for resolvable #TODO comments; suggestion cards can be started with Start or dismissed.

sources.title: Jules Scheduled Tasks
sources.locator: Creating a Scheduled Task; Managing Scheduled Tasks; Common Use Cases
sources.finding: Recurring tasks run automatically at a set frequency and cadence; three templated scheduled tasks (performance, design, security) are offered. The page says editing a scheduled task is not supported.

sources.title: Jules Integrations
sources.finding: Integrations are read-only by default, can trigger Jules from external events, and store API keys encrypted, never exposed in chat or shared between sessions.

sources.title: Jules REST API Quickstart
sources.locator: alpha note; Generate Your API Key; API concepts; Your first API call
sources.finding: The alpha REST API uses Jules API keys (at most 3) in X-Goog-Api-Key. Sessions have stable IDs; automationMode AUTO_CREATE_PR is optional (default no PR); API sessions auto-approve plans unless requirePlanApproval is true.

sources.title: Jules REST API Sessions
sources.locator: Create, List, Get, Delete a Session; Send a Message; Approve a Plan; Session States
sources.finding: Sessions can be created, listed, read, deleted, messaged and have plans approved; states are QUEUED, PLANNING, AWAITING_PLAN_APPROVAL, AWAITING_USER_FEEDBACK, IN_PROGRESS, PAUSED, COMPLETED and FAILED.

sources.title: Jules Tools Reference
sources.locator: Installation; Authentication; remote list/new/pull; Interactive Dashboard (TUI)
sources.finding: Jules Tools installs from npm, signs in with the Google account, lists repositories and remote sessions, starts sessions (optionally several in parallel) and pulls results; the TUI shows sessions and diffs.

sources.title: Jules changelog: Jules Turndown
sources.finding: Jules winds down on 2026-12-31; sessions could continue until 2026-11-11, after which Jules is read-only. Jules Tools plus a CLI-agent prompt export settings, environment variables, scheduled tasks, repositories, memories, setup scripts and every session (prompt, plan, activity log, patches) to a local folder; environment variable values are written in plaintext. The export script uses undocumented internal endpoints. Code, branches and PRs stay in GitHub.

sources.title: Jules changelog: MCP support comes to Jules
sources.finding: Jules supports only hand-selected MCP servers (Linear, Stitch, Neon, Tinybird, Context7, Supabase), each added with an API key in the user Settings page; Google limits the list deliberately for security and vets each server's permissions.

sources.title: Jules changelog: Improved Jules Critic
sources.finding: The critic agent's real-time analysis of the code is visible in the UI.

sources.title: Jules changelog: Planning Critic
sources.finding: A Planning Critic agent reviews and refines every plan that does not need human approval before execution.

sources.title: Jules changelog: REST API: Repoless, File Outputs, and Activity Filters
sources.finding: Session activities are immutable, follow an event-source pattern, can reconstruct a session and can be fetched with a createTime filter; completed sessions return the change set as a Git patch.

sources.title: Jules changelog: Use Environment Variables In Jules
sources.finding: Repository-level environment variables can be enabled per task at start; access lasts the whole task and cannot be changed after it begins.

sources.title: Jules changelog: Jules gains memory
sources.finding: Jules saves preferences, nudges and corrections per repository and uses them in later tasks there; memory can be turned on or off per repository under Knowledge.

sources.title: Jules changelog: Jules Acts on PR Feedback
sources.finding: Jules reads and responds to pull request comments and pushes commits with requested changes; Reactive Mode limits this to comments that mention @Jules.
